description:
The ground is near-black and flat, edge to edge. Centred on it, in every one of the twelve seeds, is the same construction: a vertical stack of three to five very large translucent circles and ellipses in a desaturated slate blue-grey, overlapped so their union reads as one soft-edged lozenge, peanut or gourd -- a tall rounded silhouette with shallow notches where the circles meet. It occupies most of the frame height and about half its width, leaving empty black margins left and right. It has no outline, no texture and almost no internal value change; where two circles overlap the tone lifts one step, and that is the only modelling in the piece. Over that blob, near its centre, sits a cluster of long thin translucent rectangles -- pale warm grey, like strips of tape, lath or pick-up-sticks -- rotated at assorted angles, overlapping, and brightening where they cross. In most seeds a handful of small solid mid-grey squares and diamonds sit outside the blob in the black margins near the frame edge, like debris or registration marks. That is the entire vocabulary: soft blue-grey circles, pale grey bars, small grey squares. It is not a picture of any nameable object. The nearest reading I can give it is a bundle of sticks or splints held inside a body of fog or stone -- something wrapped, with a fracture or a splint inside it, seen as an x-ray or a specimen slide.

What the twelve share is almost everything: the same slate blob in the same centred position at very nearly the same silhouette, the same pale bars, the same black ground, the same extremely narrow value range. What differs is almost entirely the bar cluster. 9369 and 10801 hold a small tight knot of short overlapping rectangles; 9011 a small tilted stack leaning left; 9548, 9727, 10085 and 10264 a dense radiating scribble that nearly fills the blob; 9190, 9906, 10443 and 10980 long splayed sticks that cross past the blob edge and read as an asterisk or jackstraws, with 10443 the thinnest and sparsest of the set. 9727 is separated less by its bars than by a column of four grey squares down its left margin and three diamonds at its right. 10622 is the outlier and does not look like it belongs to the same run: its blob is pushed down and left, its bars have become wide horizontal planks stacked like slats, and a band of dark grey squares and pentagons runs across the top and down the left side, clipped hard by the frame at the left edge and repeating again at bottom-left.

Across the three market states, on seeds 9011, 9190, 9369 and 9548, the change is almost entirely SCALE. In stress the whole blob inflates and pushes past the tile on the left, right and bottom, so the silhouette is cropped off and the tile becomes a large flat grey field; the bar cluster stays roughly the same absolute size and therefore reads proportionally smaller and more marooned, and the small marginal squares are pushed out of frame and vanish. In recovery the blob returns to about its neutral size and the marginal squares come back. Nothing cracks, darkens, shifts hue, gains or loses an element except by cropping -- it is the same drawing at a different magnification. Neutral and recovery are close: at 256px 9548 does show a genuinely re-rotated cluster with a new long diagonal at bottom-left, and 9011 gains a bar, but 9190 and 9369 differ only by a slight scale and jitter. Same seed across three states is unmistakably the same token; the risk on this sheet is the opposite one, that two of the three states are too alike to tell apart.

At 120px the silhouette survives and the pale cluster survives as a smudge, but the individual bars merge into one another. The blob, which is the great majority of the visual mass, is effectively constant across all twelve, so what a browser sees twelve times is the same grey lozenge on black with a pale mark in the middle of it. The twelve resolve into about four recognisable kinds at that size rather than twelve: a tiny knot (9369, 10801, 9011), a dense scribble mass (9548, 9727, 10085, 10264), long crossing sticks (9190, 9906, 10443, 10980), and the collage-like 10622. The small marginal squares turn out to be what most reliably separates one tile from its neighbour at browse size, which is a strange job for the least considered element in the frame to be doing. On the 120px state sheet, stress is legible as different because the blob is larger and clipped, while neutral and recovery are hard to tell apart for 9011, 9190 and 9369.

Contrast is very low throughout -- pale grey on mid blue-grey on near-black -- and the bars against the blob are the only place with real separation. There is essentially no chroma: one cool grey, one warm grey. Artefacts I can see: the stress row clips the blob at three edges in every seed, which reads as scale overflow rather than as an intention; 10622 clips its dark tile band mid-shape at the left edge; marginal squares in 9906 and 10980 sit half off the frame; and in several seeds (10264, 9906, 9190) the bars run past the blob into the black with no acknowledgement, so the blob reads as a backdrop the bars are not actually inside rather than as a body containing them.
